analysis:
Change (SSDPrefixCache.swift head 1794-1800, base 1794-1799): retireIndexedEntries now calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices, taking removalLock per slice instead of holding it for the whole URL batch. Each slice still re-checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot under the lock before SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. Lock granularity is finer, but every unlink still passes the same safety/ownership gate. performIndexedRemoval (base 2011-2016) already documents that successor-rebuild races are tolerated (SSDCacheEpochStore.removeStaleBlock).

Callers in the visible units: sweepExpiredEntries (base 1848-1855) passes TTL-expired URLs, and budget eviction and corrupt-drop are also documented callers. The T-041 TTL/LRU mitigations are unchanged in kind. Whether the sweep stops partway now depends on removeInSlices semantics.

Unverified contracts, outside the supplied evidence (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift is not supplied):
- What a slice returning nil (ownership lost or unsafe root) does to the merged Result: does it stop processing or keep going?
- How removed and externalChange are aggregated across slices.
- The slice size.

A lost-ownership mid-batch stop is acceptable: the successor wipes the root. A silent continue would also be guarded per slice. No regression was identified against T-041 at-rest/TTL purge, A-001, or the staging-reservation paths. The head lookup and endAdoption code (head 486-652) and close() are unchanged per the range map.

Integration should confirm the removeInSlices aggregation, and that no partial-result path causes a TTL-expired file to remain both indexed and readable beyond the TTL.
